sentences.text: have assailed the common judgment dated 14.09.2016 in NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB MVC Nos.820/2015 and 821/2015 which were disposed of along with another connected MVC No.817/2015 passed by the IV Addl. District Judge and MACT-XIII, Vijaypura.
2. By filing these appeals, the appellants are claiming enhancement in the compensation so awarded by the Tribunal.
3. The parties to these appeals are referred with reference to their rank before the Tribunal.

4. The facts of the case are that, the claimants in MVC No.820/2015 and 821/2015 filed the petitions along with other aforesaid petition claiming compensation on account of death of Saipan Shaikh @
Lavane and Sadik S/o Bande Ali Shaikh @ Lavane in a road traffic accident that took place on 11.05.2005 at 12.15 p.m. on Solapur - Akkalkot Road, near Valasang village, when the deceased Saipan was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.MH- 13/BM-5675 along with pillion rider by name Sadik towards Akkalkot side.

It is alleged that the driver of NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB Tanker Lorry bearing No.MH-46/F-2797 by driving his lorry from opposite side in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the said motorcycle in which the aforesaid two persons sustained fatal injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

sentences.text: The claimants specifically stated in their respective petitions that, the deceased in the said accident were the only bread earners in their respective families.

It is further stated that the deceased Saipan Shaikh was working as Driver and he had monthly income of Rs.10,000/- and the deceased Sadik Shaikh was doing Coolie and Centering work and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.

It is alleged that, because of death of these two earning members in the family, the claimants in both the appeals have suffered lot, therefore, they filed claim petitions before the Tribunal seeking compensation with interest at the rate of 18% per annum as prayed in the petition.

Before the Tribunal, the Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and resisted the petitions by filing detail objections statement, denying the entire averments made in the claim petitions in toto.
It is contended that the accident has taken place because of rash and negligent riding of the motorbike by deceased Saipan.
It is submitted that income stated in both the petitions is highly excessive and the claim is also excessive and there is violation of the policy conditions.
Therefore, it is prayed by the Insurance Company to dismiss the petitions.
7. Insofar as respondent No.1 is concerned, he appeared before the Tribunal and filed his written statement.
He admitted ownership of Tanker Lorry bearing No.MH-46/F-2797, except this fact, he denied all other averments.
He further contended that the Tribunal has no jurisdiction to try these petitions, as the accident has occurred in Maharashtra.
Based on the rival contentions of both the parties, relevant issues were framed by the Tribunal.

9. To substantiate their claim, wife of deceased Sadik was examined as PW1, wife of deceased Saipan was examined as PW2 and also two other witnesses were examined on behalf of the claimants as PWs.3 and 4 and documents at Exs.P1 to P12 with the respective signatures were marked.

On behalf of respondents no oral evidence was adduced, but copy of Insurance Police was marked as Ex.R1.
10.

The Tribunal on hearing the arguments on both sides and on evaluation of the oral and documentary evidence available on record has awarded compensation of Rs.9,43,000/- to the claimants in MVC No.820/2015 and awarded compensation of Rs.10,39,000/- to the claimants in MVC No.821/2015 with directions about apportionment and investment, and directed respondent No.2 - Insurance Company to deposit the same with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization, NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB holding that both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
11. Dissatisfied with the award amount, the claimants in both the petitions are before this Court in their respective appeals seeking enhancement of the compensation.
12. Heard learned counsel for the parties in both appeals.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the claimants in both the appeals submit that, while assessing the compensation, the Tribunal though observed that the claimants in both the petitions claimed income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month and they were contributing the same for family maintenance, but assessed monthly income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/-, which is quite meager.
Hence, they submit that, the assessment of the income of the deceased in both claim petitions by the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB Tribunal is incorrect and it required to be enhanced reasonably.

14. As against this submission, learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company submits that whatever compensation awarded in both the claims petitions is proper and do not call for any interference by this Court.
15. We have given our anxious consideration to the submissions of both sides and perused the records.
16. So far as death of deceased Saipan and Sadik in road traffic accident that occurred on 11.05.2005 at about 12.15 p.m., is not in dispute.

It is also not in dispute that deceased Saipan was aged 32 years and deceased Sadik was aged 22 years at the time of accident, as per the post mortem report produced at Exs.P9 and P1.
17.

In view of the rival submissions from both sides, the only point that would arise for our consideration is:
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB Whether the claimants in MVC Nos.820/2015 and 821/2015 have made out grounds to enhance the compensation as prayed for?
18.

Insofar as avocation of the deceased Saipan S/o. Bande Ali is concerned, he was a Driver by profession and according to the claimants, the deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- per month, but no document is produced.
In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal has taken into consideration the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/-.
But in our opinion, the said notional income taken by the Tribunal is incorrect in view of the Circular issued by the Karnataka Legal Services Authority.

Therefore, considering the year of accident and his profession as Driver, as per the Chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority if Rs.8,000/- is taken as monthly income of the deceased, it would meet the ends of justice.

As per the judgment of Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, as the claimants - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB in this appeal have lost the bread earner in the family, as he was just 32 years, 40% of the Rs.8,000/- i.e., Rs.3,200/- is to be added to his monthly income which comes to Bande Ali And Ors vs Santosh And Anr on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85017543/
6 Rs.11,200/-.

sentences.text: As the deceased was a married person, having three dependents, as per the decision in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) 1/3rd of the income i.e., Rs.3,733/- is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then it comes to Rs.7,467/-.
Further, as the deceased was aged 32 years at the time of his death, appropriate multiplier i.e., applicable as per Schedule is '16'.

Thus, loss of dependency works out to (Rs.7,467/- x 12 x 16) Rs.14,33,664/-.
19.

There are three dependents and towards loss of consortium Rs.40,000/- each is to be awarded,
which comes to Rs.1,20,000/-.

So far as loss of estate, funeral expenses and transportation of dead body are concerned, as per the judgment in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), in altogether if Rs.30,000/- is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice and accordingly it is awarded.
- 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB 20.

22.
Insofar as the appellants-claimants in MFA No.201322/2017 are concerned, it is not in dispute that they are wife and parents of the deceased Sadik.

It is the case of the claimants that by doing Coolie and Centering work, the deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- per month,

which is on the lower side.

sentences.text:
Further,
as per the judgment in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), as the claimants in this appeal have lost the bread earner in the family and as he was aged just 22 years at the time of death, the future prospects also has to be added at 40% of his monthly income which comes to Rs.3,200/-.
Thus, total monthly income comes to Rs.8,000/- + Rs.3,200/- = Rs.11,200/-.

As the deceased was a married person, his wife and parents are dependents, 1/3rd of his income i.e., Rs.3,733/-, is to be deducted towards his personal expenses as per the judgment in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), then it comes to Rs.7,467/-.
The appropriate multiplier i.e., applicable to the age of deceased as per Schedule is '18'.

Thus, loss of - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB dependency is calculated at Rs.7,467/- x 12 x 18 = Rs.16,12,872/-.
23.
As there are three dependents, towards loss of consortium Rs.40,000/- each is to be awarded which comes to Rs.1,20,000/-.

So far as loss of estate, funeral expenses and transportation of death body are concerned, as per the judgment in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), in altogether if Rs.30,000/- is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

24. Thus, the claimants in MFA No.201322/20212 are held entitled for compensation under the following heads:
Sl.
 Heads Amount No 1 Loss of dependency Rs.16,12,872/-

2 Loss of consortium Rs.1,20,000/-
 (Rs.40,000/- x 5)

3 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
4 Towards funeral expenses & Rs.15,000/-
 transportation of dead body  Total Rs.17,62,872/-
 - 16 -  NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB 25.
The Tribunal has awarded total compensation Rs.10,39,000/-.
If out of the total compensation awarded by this Court, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is deducted, it comes to Rs.7,23,872/-.
Thus, claimants in this appeal are held entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,23,872/-.

Insofar as rate of interest is concerned, though the claimants have claimed 18%
interest, there is no material to grant the same.
The Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petitions.

The same is just and proper and do not call for any interference.
27.
The Insurance Company has not preferred any appeal on the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, since, as on the date of accident policy was in force.
That means, so far as question of liability is concerned, it has attained finality.
Hence, the Insurance - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB Company is directed to indemnify the entire compensation amount in both matters.

28. It is brought to the notice of this Court by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that in MFA No.201322/2017, it is ordered that the claimants are not entitled for the interest on the compensation amount for the period between 08.01.2018 to 09.01.2024.
The submission is taken on record.

29. Resultantly, we pass the following:
ORDER (i) Both the appeals are allowed in part with costs.

(ii) The appellants-claimants in MFA No.201323/2017 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.15,83,664/- as against Rs.9,43,000/- awarded by the Tribunal with interest @ 6% per annum and the appellants are - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.6,40,664/-.

(iii) The appellants-claimants in MFA No.201322/2017 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.17,62,872/- as against Rs.10,39,000/- awarded by the Tribunal with interest @ 6% per annum (excluding interest for the period between 08.01.2018 and 09.01.2024 as submitted).
The appellants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,23,872/-.
(iv) The respondent No.2- Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest at the rate of 6% per annum within four weeks from today in both the appeals.

So far as appellants in MFA No.201322/2017 it is held that, they - 19 - Bande Ali And Ors vs Santosh And Anr on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85017543/
9 NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB are not entitled for interest on the enhanced compensation amount for the period from 08.01.2018 to 09.01.2024.

Insofar as avocation of the deceased Saipan S/o. Bande Ali is concerned, he was a Driver by profession and according to the claimants, the deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- per month, but no document is produced.
In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal has taken into consideration the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/-.
But in our opinion, the said notional income taken by the Tribunal is incorrect in view of the Circular issued by the Karnataka Legal Services Authority.
Therefore, considering the year of accident and his profession as Driver, as per the Chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority if Rs.8,000/- is taken as monthly income of the deceased, it would meet the ends of justice.
Insofar as rate of interest is concerned, though the claimants have claimed 18%
interest, there is no material to grant the same.
The Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petitions.
The same is just and proper and do not call for any interference.
27.
The Insurance Company has not preferred any appeal on the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, since, as on the date of accident policy was in force.
That means, so far as question of liability is concerned, it has attained finality.
Hence, the Insurance - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5947-DB Company is directed to indemnify the entire compensation amount in both matters.
